question: One day after undergoing surgery for a traumatic right pelvic fracture, a 73-year-old man has pain over his buttocks and scrotum and urinary incontinence. Physical examination shows right-sided perineal hypesthesia and absence of anal sphincter contraction when the skin around the anus is touched. This patient is most likely to have which of the following additional neurological deficits?

enhanced_information: The patient is likely to have an additional neurological deficit of absent reflex erection. The presence of absence of anal sphincter contraction and right-sided perineal hypesthesia indicates involvement of the S2-S4 nerve roots, which commonly leads to this specific deficit.
analysis: The patient's symptoms of right-sided perineal hypesthesia, absence of anal sphincter contraction, and urinary incontinence following a traumatic right pelvic fracture suggest involvement of the S2-S4 nerve roots. Given this pattern, the most likely additional neurological deficit would be an absent reflex erection, as this specific deficit commonly occurs with S2-S4 nerve root involvement.
